content.what_it_is: Python (numpy/matplotlib) port of the inlet_shoal bathymetry plot, written for a postprocessing workshop. Loads dep_shoal_inlet.txt from a hard-coded user desktop path (L10, with comments L8-L9 telling the user to substitute their own path and noting '/' vs '\\' path separators). Gets n,m via np.shape (L13), dx=dy=2.0 (L14-L15), builds x and y coordinate arrays by list comprehension (L17-L18). Defines sponge outline x 0-180 (L21-L22) and wavemaker outline x 240-260 (L24-L25) using y[len(y)-1] for the full y extent. Creates a 6x5 inch dpi=200 figure (L29-L35), plots pcolor of -1*dep with cmap='terrain' (L37), tight axis and labels (L38-L40), plt.hold(True) (L41), overlays sponge and wavemaker as black dashed/solid lines with white rotated text labels (L44-L47), adds a colorbar labeled 'Bathymetry (m)' (L50-L51), and saves inlet__shoal_bathy.png (L54).

equations.expr: x = np.asarray([float(xa)*dx for xa in range(m)])
y = np.asarray([float(ya)*dy for ya in range(n)])

unresolved: ax created at L34 is never used; all plotting goes through plt state calls
plt.hold(True) (L41) was removed in matplotlib 3.0, so the script targets an older matplotlib; version requirement is not stated
the load path directory is spelled 'Intel_Shoal' (L10) versus the case name inlet_shoal; output filename has a double underscore 'inlet__shoal_bathy.png' (L54)
